INCONSISTENCY_1_deposited_artifact_is_no.consequence: the file I deposited as evidence for the environment lock does not reproduce the package component of the digest sitting in Appendix B. Root verified the artifact is internally consistent -- it is; it is simply not evidence for the promoted value.
INCONSISTENCY_1_deposited_artifact_is_no.finding: environment_lock.txt is sorted by name.lower(); the package list hashed INTO the promoted digest is sorted by the (Name, version) tuple. The two orderings are NOT identical on this host.
INCONSISTENCY_1_deposited_artifact_is_no.severity: the same failure shape as the profile digest: an artifact that looks like evidence for a promoted number and is not.

INCONSISTENCY_2_promoted_digest_uses_a_n.consequence: a reader applying the project convention -- as root did -- gets a different number and reasonably concludes the value is wrong. It is not wrong; it is non-conforming.
INCONSISTENCY_2_promoted_digest_uses_a_n.finding: 842a7a19... is sha256 over Python's DEFAULT json.dumps separators, while this repository has one canonical JSON convention (lab_common.canonical_json, compact) used by every other digest in the freeze path.
INCONSISTENCY_2_promoted_digest_uses_a_n.my_view: it should be re-derived under canonical_json and amended three-way with the old value preserved, so every digest in the freeze path shares one serialization. I have NOT done that: it changes a value in the pre-registration document and is root decision.

deposited_artifact.derivation: name==version lines sorted by name.lower(), WITH a trailing newline
deposited_artifact.where: results/live_ab/environment_lock.txt, the file root independently verified

package_list_inside_that_object.derivation: name==version lines sorted by the (Name, version) TUPLE, joined with newlines, NO trailing newline

whole_environment.covers: the entire environment_lock object: interpreter version, tokenized path, implementation, packages_sha256, packages_count, packages_source, numpy version and notes

deterministic_derivation.step_1: take the preparation manifest's environment_lock object verbatim
deterministic_derivation.step_2: serialize with json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True) using PYTHON DEFAULT separators (', ' and ': '), NOT compact

exact_preimage_bytes.note: the literal bytes that were hashed, deposited so anyone can recompute without reconstructing my script

not_withdrawn_and_why: my stated default was withdrawal if the preimage proved unreconstructible. It IS reconstructible, so withdrawing would destroy a recoverable value. The two inconsistencies are reported for a ruling instead.
outcome: REPRODUCED. The value is derivable; two real inconsistencies surfaced in the process.
